s1.syndrome_frame: Painful oral mass with bone destruction and atypical cells
salient_findings: 10-mm polypoid mass on the left lower gingiva
Rough-surfaced polypoid lesion with whitish pseudomembrane
Moth-eaten pattern of mandibular bone resorption on panoramic radiography
Atypical spindle and pleomorphic cells on biopsy
key_facts: 69-year-old Japanese man
History of chemoradiotherapy for squamous cell carcinoma of the left buccal mucosa 15 years earlier
No tobacco or alcohol use
Trismus present
Normal vital signs
Intraoral inspection revealed rough-surfaced polypoid lesion
Biopsy specimen showed loose granulation tissue with scattered atypical cells
Spindle cells had basophilic cytoplasm, bizarre nuclei, and atypical mitoses
Immunohistochemical staining positive for vimentin, α-smooth muscle actin, p63, p53, and CD68
Ki-67 labeling index approximately 50%

differentials: Clear cell sarcoma of soft tissue

shortlist.label: Sarcomatoid squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of squamous cell carcinoma and presence of atypical spindle cells

shortlist.label: Spindle cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of spindle cells with basophilic cytoplasm and atypical mitoses

shortlist.label: Malignant fibrous histiocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of atypical cells and positive immunohistochemical staining for vimentin and CD68

shortlist.label: Undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of atypical spindle and pleomorphic cells with high Ki-67 labeling index

shortlist.label: Inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of loose granulation tissue and inflammatory cells with positive immunohistochemical staining for α-smooth muscle actin

raw.rationale: The patient's history of chemoradiotherapy for squamous cell carcinoma and the presence of atypical spindle cells with positive immunohistochemical staining for p63 and p53, which are often expressed in squamous cell carcinomas, support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Spindle cell carcinoma
rejected.why: While the biopsy shows spindle cell morphology, the clinical context and immunohistochemical profile more strongly suggest a sarcomatoid transformation of a squamous cell carcinoma
